newsitem.title: FRANCE: French old-crop wheat prices fall on farm selling.
newsitem.headline: French old-crop wheat prices fall on farm selling.

text.p: Old-crop wheat prices were sharply lower on Thursday as farmers' selling intensified ahead of the new crop, dealers said. But trade remained limited to small volumes, they said.
Barley was steady in Rouen but lower elsewhere in sympathy with wheat while maize trade was subdued as both sellers and buyers were sidelined.
Rouen wheat for May delivery was bid at 845 francs per tonne, excluding carry. The same period fetched 857.50 on Wednesday.
May wheat into the southwestern port of La Pallice was bid at 860 francs per tonne and offered at 865 francs francs per tonne, down 20 francs on Wednesday.
"It is a fast and strong decline. It is too quick and too strong," one dealer said.

Old-crop fob Atlantic maize was quoted at 835-840 francs, unchanged on Wednesday. Operators await the results of the first tender for the preferential import of 150,000 tonnes of non-EU maize into Portugal.
May-June barley into Rouen was offered at 855 francs per tonne, unchanged on Wednesday but Fob-Moselle barley for May-June delivery was offered at 820 francs, down 10 francs.

Traders bidding through France asked to export 153,700 tonnes of European Union barley at rebates ranging from 14.49 to 19.94 Ecus per tonne at this week's grain auction. The lowest subsidy bid for barley covers the export of only 10,000 tonnes, traders said.
Exporters hope the EU will grant a subsidy of 16 Ecus which would cover the export of up to 76,000 tonnes of barley in France.

French domestic grains are traded on a "July basis," reflecting their underlying value without the twice-monthly carrying charges which must also be added for delivery periods between August 1 and the end of each July/June crop year.
